name: phase_checklist_created

why: tasks are a progress mirror + recovery anchor; gating behavior on TaskList state would recreate the dual-authority drift class

name: recovery_uses_tasklist_anchor
why: compaction recovery gets a structured position anchor before re-deriving from prose, but files win on disagreement

name: skipped_phases_marked_not_deleted
why: a silently-deleted checklist item is indistinguishable from a silently-skipped phase

name: deep_dive_dispatch_exists
why: v3.0.0 re-altitudes Phase 1.5's analytical bulk into one dispatched design deep-dive agent on the think tier

name: deep_dive_reads_models_think
why: the deep-dive dispatch reads models.think from config and passes model: <value> only when non-empty (never a literal)

name: deep_dive_dossier_goes_to_research_draft
why: the deep-dive extends the existing compaction-checkpoint file rather than inventing a new artifact

name: viability_decision_authority_stays_in_shell
pattern: viability decision authority stays with the shell|pre-assessment is analysis, not a decision
why: the user-facing viability gate decision never moves into the dispatched agent — the agent only pre-assesses

name: deep_dive_has_inline_fallback
pattern: Fallback \(dispatch failed|fall back to running the .phase-1-research\.md. protocol .{0,20}inline
why: if the deep-dive dispatch fails or returns an unusable dossier, the shell falls back to the pre-4.0 inline research path

name: question_design_ref_exists
why: v3.3.0 question redesign: the confidence gate / rulebook / kill-list authority file must exist

name: skill_points_to_question_design
why: Phase 1, 1.5b, and the Rules section route how-to-ask discipline to question-design.md

name: concurrent_deep_dive_dispatch
why: v3.3.0 speed: the design deep-dive is seeded in the background at Phase 0.6 so its no-user-input passes overlap the Phase-1 conversation

name: deep_dive_handoff_via_sendmessage
why: the concurrent deep-dive gets the Phase-1 summary via SendMessage once the conversation finishes; synchronous dispatch is the documented fallback

name: bulk_ask_single_call_rule
why: Round 1 bulk understanding asks everything remaining in at most one AskUserQuestion call of up to 4 questions

name: confidence_gate_wired
why: the confidence gate (HIGH decide-and-inform / MEDIUM-LOW ask) replaces the old 'never assume technical decisions' rule

name: kill_list_referenced
why: 'Don't ask obvious questions' now points at the question-design.md kill-list

name: assumed_logging_wired
why: HIGH-tier decisions are logged as ASSUMED: in the Decision Log and read back in Phase 5's ASSUMPTIONS MADE section

name: phase5_assumptions_made_section
why: Phase 5 approval summary surfaces all ASSUMED decisions as one cheap audit point with 'flag any to change before approval'

name: round_budget_stated
why: the 15 phases collapse into a 4-5 interruption-round budget with ≤5 asks through Phases 1-2

name: round2_challenge_viability_merged
pattern: fuses the challenge with the Phase 2 viability echo
why: Round 2 merges the 1.5b challenge and the mandatory Phase 2 viability echo into one AskUserQuestion call

name: round3_consolidated_post_spec
why: Phases 3.5/3.7/3.8/4.5 keep their tasks but merge their interruption points into one consolidated call

name: concurrent_critic_dispatch
why: the 4.95 critic runs concurrently with composing the Phase 5 summary; findings are reconciled before asking

name: detailed_topic_proceeds_with_assumption
pattern: Do NOT ask a standalone confirmation|proceed into NEW mode immediately with a stated assumption
why: the detailed-topic heuristic (two-way door) proceeds into NEW with a stated assumption instead of costing a confirmation round; CAPTURE/EPIC still confirm

name: idea_graduation_uses_cli_with_to
why: v3.6.0 wave 2: idea graduation (status + graduated_to) routes through the CLI in one atomic call instead of a hand-Edit. Un-targeted 'contains' check scans SKILL.md + references/ (per eval-run.py's check_skill_assertions — verified: contains checks rglob every *.md under the skill dir except SKILL.md itself, in addition to SKILL.md), so this single assertion covers both the SKILL.md:646 site and references/phase-finalize.md's steps 3 + 'Idea graduation target' section.

name: uses_lock_acquire_planning
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: the Session Mutex Check routes through shipyard-data lock acquire instead of hand-Read/Write.

name: uses_lock_release
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: mutex release (Phase 6 finalize, IDEA-CAPTURE mode) routes through shipyard-data lock release instead of a hand Write.

name: no_hand_write_lock_file
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: skill-mutex lock files are CLI-owned — no skill body hand-Writes them anymore.

name: consolidated_approval_covers_ac_scope_spec
pattern: approves the acceptance scenarios as written.*scope.*approves the spec
why: v3.8.0: the consolidated gate's Approve-everything option must cover all three things it replaces — AC sign-off, scope-drift check, and spec approval — in one option description.

name: render_before_ask_rule_in_question_design
why: v3.8.0: the render-before-ask rule's canonical definition lives in question-design.md — verified the assertion schema supports a ref: target the same way ship-review's not_contains checks target ref:pipeline-cursor.md.

name: render_before_ask_inline_rule
why: v3.8.0: ship-discuss's own Rules section restates the render-before-ask one-liner inline (every command skill that asks gets this, not just discuss).

name: has_think_override_flag
why: v3.9.0: per-invocation think-tier override, parsed from $ARGUMENTS.

name: emits_think_override_used_event
why: v3.9.0: emits shipyard-data events emit think_override_used model=<m> once at first use of the override.

name: has_spawn_failure_fallback
why: v3.9.0: if a think-tier dispatch errors at spawn because the model is unavailable, fall back to models.think and re-dispatch, printed as one line.

name: render_provenance_negation
why: v3.11.0 context-conflation fix: the render-before-ask rule must state the negative — Read results, subagent returns, dossier files, and SendMessage payloads are not 'shown to the user'. Anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires.

name: render_before_ask_negation_in_question_design
why: v3.11.0: the canonical rule in question-design.md § 'Render before asking' states the provenance negation — context-only content (Read/dossier/subagent return) is not rendered.

name: option_packing_does_not_count
why: v3.11.0: packing tradeoffs into AskUserQuestion question/option strings is explicitly named as not-rendering (the UI shows a compact card).

name: no_weak_render_verbs_at_ask_rounds
why: v3.11.0: Rounds 1-3 used weak verbs that permitted blind asks; the confirmed Round-3 blind ask fired off a 21KB dossier Read with zero chat text. Rendering language must be explicit ('render as chat text'), not 'fold in naturally'.

name: round3_renders_before_single_ask
why: v3.11.0: Round 3's consolidated decision ask must render the dossier-derived decision items as chat text before the one AskUserQuestion.

name: scenario_render_rule_in_question_design
why: v3.14.0: the scenario-render default (render a concrete example scenario above every non-trivial discuss ask; escalate to both-sides for hard/one-way-door questions; skip only genuinely self-evident asks) is canonical in question-design.md. Pins the anchor phrase so the behavior can't silently regress the way the v3.11.0 blind-ask class did when render rules were prose-only.

name: phase_1_5b_renders_mini_story_per_item
why: v3.14.0: Phase 1.5b's challenge block must give each item a one-line example scenario (mini-story, rule Q9) above the ask, not just the finding summary line.

name: phase_2_renders_primary_use_scenario
why: v3.14.0: the Phase 2 viability echo renders the primary use scenario as chat text so 'does this match your intent?' is answered against a concrete flow, not the abstract gate labels.

name: round3_renders_before_after_example
why: v3.14.0: Round-3 impact ripples that change existing behavior carry a before/after example scenario, and simplification candidates a today-vs-lib example — extending the scenario-render default past Phase 1/Phase 5 into the middle rounds.

name: estimates_never_asked
why: Estimates (RICE, story points, etc.) are Shipyard-decided, never surfaced as an AskUserQuestion — closes the story-points-ask bad-ask incident.

name: estimates_no_ask_user_question_for_estimate_fields
why: The old explicit instruction permitting AskUserQuestion for RICE fields must not regress back in.

name: kill_list_bans_estimation
why: Kill-list item 9 bans asking the user to produce story points, RICE components, or other analysis-derivable numbers.

name: kill_list_bans_orchestration_asks
why: Kill-list item 10 bans asking whether to wait for/skip/retry the skill's own background dispatches — closes the wait-for-critique bad-ask incident.

name: backlog_reeval_decide_and_inform
why: RICE re-scoring in backlog re-evaluation is decide-and-inform (rendered + ASSUMED-logged), not an AskUserQuestion approval. Step 1's dependency-edge AskUserQuestion is untouched and lives elsewhere in this file.

name: phase_15_wait_semantics
pattern: waiting is never a user decision
why: CI-pinned, do not reword. Phase 1.5 (deep-dive) and Phase 4.95 (critic) both state that waiting on background work is never a user decision/AskUserQuestion — closes the wait-for-critique/wait-for-dossier bad-ask incident.

name: phase_495_wait_semantics_count
pattern: waiting is never a user decision.*waiting is never a user decision
why: CI-pinned, do not reword. Pins that the wait-semantics phrase appears at BOTH join points (Phase 1.5 and Phase 4.95), not just one.
